summary_md: Chen, Wilder, Qiu, An, Rice and Tambe (IJCAI-23) study seed selection when adoption follows complex contagion: under their K-complex model a node activates with probability p0 once at least K neighbours are active and p1 otherwise. They prove the objective is non-submodular and NP-hard, then frame seeding as an MDP solved by Double-DQN (RL4CCIM). Four additions address sparse rewards: solution filtering to nodes near a degree-K hub, reward-prioritised replay, a global marginal-contribution reward and a GAT encoder. On nine small networks with deterministic cascades (p0=1, p1=0, budget T=8 or 12), RL4CCIM has the best normalised influence everywhere, sometimes tied. Greedy collapses on India (0.0396 vs 0.5347). RL4CCIM matches the MIP optimum on DC and DOSIM and comes within about 6 to 8 percent elsewhere. In the India ablation, the drops are 10.2 to 35.2 percent. There are no field data: cascades are simulated, and scale is the stated limit. For Paul's system the paper does not supply an estimate. It is a warning about an assumption. The coalition engines (budget frontier, per-topic coalition, dashboard budget recruit) run a simple-contagion independent-cascade kernel and greedy or knee logic justified by diminishing returns. If real cosponsor joining is threshold-like, as the LT priming module already assumes one target at a time, those greedy paths can miss jointly valuable seed sets. They would also drop candidates whose solo marginal is zero. The useful takeaway is a test, not a method swap: measure whether CU-bill join hazards jump with the count of already-joined close partners. Until that is checked, read greedy guarantees as properties of the model kernel only. This bearing analysis is UNVERIFIED per DE-062.

bearings.paper_claim: Complex-contagion IM is non-submodular (Thm 1) and NP-hard (Thm 2); greedy seeding can be arbitrarily bad, scoring 0.0396 normalised influence on India (202 nodes) vs 0.5347 for RL4CCIM and 0.0293 vs 0.5585 on Exhibition, deterministic setting p0=1, p1=0, T=8 or 12.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 3 PDF p3; Table 1 and Sec. 6.1 PDF p7
bearings.system_side: The frontier runs lazy greedy over up to 60 seeds on an independent-cascade kernel, stops as soon as the best marginal is zero, and reads a diminishing-returns knee (last seed with 4 x gain at least peak). Both the stop rule and the knee presume submodular spread; under threshold adoption, zero early marginals would end the path before complementary seeds pay off.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Bites only if real cosponsorship joining is threshold-like (join probability jumps with count of already-joined partners). Under the system's own per-edge IC kernel the greedy logic is internally coherent; the paper tests simulated cascades on non-legislative networks only.

bearings.paper_claim: Credit sparseness: in the 8-node toy (K=3, T=4) only 17 of 70 four-seed sets (24.3 percent) activate anyone, and seed sequence {1,2,3,5} earns per-step rewards 1,1,1,2, so a seed's value shows only alongside specific other seeds.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 1 PDF p2; Sec. 5.1 PDF p4
bearings.system_side: The coalition allocator scores each of the top-45 neutral candidates by solo marginal spread, keeps only those with marginal above zero, water-fills money by marginal x (1 + 0.8 bpf), and justifies the joint report by asserting spread is submodular. It already prints joint gain beside naive-additive gain per topic.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The existing joint vs naive-additive printout is a free superadditivity detector: joint above naive-additive on any topic would signal complementarity the solo-marginal ranking cannot see. Meaningful only if the kernel or data admit threshold effects; under pure IC joint stays at or below naive-additive.

bearings.paper_claim: K-complex model (Eq. 1): activation probability p0 when at least K neighbours are active, p1 much smaller otherwise; motivated by Centola-Macy 2007 and Centola 2010 social-reinforcement evidence, but not validated on field adoption data in this paper.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 3 Eq. 1 PDF p3; Sec. 1 PDF p1
bearings.system_side: LT priming is already a deterministic threshold model: tier theta 0.6 to 3.0 plus lean and Opponent-cell terms, closed by summed pro-neighbour pressure P[u][v] x cross-cue factor plus money. It solves each target alone and one hop deep, so it never exploits the multi-target complementarity the paper optimises, and its thresholds are fixed design constants.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paper adds support only for the modelling choice that adoption can be threshold-like; it gives no estimate of K or thresholds for legislators. Joint priming across targets would be a new model needing owner authorisation and a holdout look.

bearings.paper_claim: The (1-1/e) greedy guarantee of Kempe et al. 2003 holds only for submodular IC/LT; under complex contagion no such guarantee exists and approximation is NP-hard even on simplified networks (citing Schoenebeck-Tao 2019).
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 1-2 PDF pp. 1-2; Sec. 3 PDF p3
bearings.system_side: The dashboard budget-recruit mode states it keeps the (1-1/e) guarantee because its coverage objective 1 - prod(1 - p) is monotone submodular; the closed-cascade route beside it is already labelled a non-submodular heuristic with no (1-1/e) claim.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The guarantee is true of the coverage proxy, not of real recruitment; dashboard wording should say so if threshold joining is plausible. No change to code is implied.

bearings.paper_claim: Standard IC and LT make activation probability independent of how many neighbours are active, which is what keeps them submodular; complex contagion breaks this.
bearings.system_side: build_P sets each edge probability as x/(x+6) with x = w x cpf x receiver edge_mult, independent of how many in-neighbours are already active; there is no seniority or leadership term in the kernel.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Context only: the paper offers no legislative estimate. Any count-dependent kernel would be a new model and must not merge the two cpf physics.

gaps_exposed: No test of simple vs complex contagion in cosponsorship: join hazard on CU bills as a function of the number of already-joined close partners (exposure curve) has not been measured.
Greedy paths in the budget frontier and per-topic coalition have no exact or exhaustive baseline on a small topic to bound their optimality gap if spread were non-submodular.
Candidates with zero solo marginal are dropped before allocation (per_topic_coalition.py:116); seeds valuable only in combination are invisible by construction.
The frontier knee is read as diminishing returns; a flat-then-jump curve, which threshold adoption produces, would be misread as an early knee or stop.
No source-status (leadership or rank) term in the cascade kernel, the gap Paul's margin note raises; the paper's homogeneous K does not fill it.
flags: No conflict with D-025, D-021 or the rejected SNA proposals: the paper argues for neither dropping regular cosponsorship edges nor per-edge volume normalisation, and uses no LDA data.
All bearings above are agent analysis and stay UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces them (DE-062).
Any count-dependent cascade variant must keep the two cpf physics separate (architecture rule); this paper does not justify merging them.

Paper-internal issues: SPY OPT 0.5522 is reported although the MIP is said to exceed 12 hours from SPY onward; 24.3 vs 24.2 percent effective-solution figures; ablation text says three components while listing four.
Paul's only note is truncated mid-word (as varia), so its full intent cannot be confirmed.
paul_alignment: Paul's entry has no takeaways or system links; his one margin note questions diminishing returns for high-ranking members and ties pressure susceptibility to some variable. That instinct agrees with the paper's central point that seed value need not diminish, though the paper models it through neighbour-count thresholds with homogeneous K, not node status. The note is not stale: the system as built still assumes diminishing returns in the budget frontier knee and coalition ranking, and its kernel has no leadership term.

related.why: RL4IM from that paper is the base architecture and a baseline here; the system's seed gate cites the contingency-aware idea from the same group.
Cited as related RL work on influence maximization with learned graph sampling (Kamarthi et al.).
Deep RL for influence maximization; the dashboard closed-cascade route follows RELINK and is labelled non-submodular, the same regime this paper treats.
Graph neural encoders for influence maximization, parallel to the GAT encoder here.
The system's competitive IC cascade follows Bharathi et al.; this paper shows what greedy loses once cascades are threshold-based rather than IC.
Threshold models for competitive influence, the competitive counterpart to the K-complex threshold model here.
The joint optimizer reports a Golovin-Krause bound that presumes (adaptive) submodularity; this paper marks the regime where that premise fails.
Also challenges greedy influence maximization, from the heuristic-centrality side rather than RL.
Efficient IM under submodular IC, the setting whose guarantees this paper shows do not carry to complex contagion.
Survey of behaviour-aware IM methods that situates threshold and contingency-aware seeding.
